questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-9{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the distance between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2-2)^{2}+(3-0)^{2}+(5-5)^{2}+(4-0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+9+0+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}25 & 0 \\ 0 & 25\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 \\ 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 \\ 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$  

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot 7+(-1)\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{7}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{5}^{2}}\sqrt{{7}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{50}{\sqrt{75}\sqrt{50}} \\  & =\frac{25\cdot 2}{\sqrt{25\cdot 3}\sqrt{25\cdot 2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})≈{35.26}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -6 & 18\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+0\cdot (-1)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
